evidence: commit 5527354 -- Task 9 (F7 closed: mls-verifier federated to its own environment:verify subject)
assertion.rationale: F7: anything executing inside a verify job — a compromised action, a malicious transitive dependency pulled by npm ci, a tampered audit script — could read the job-scoped ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL/TOKEN, mint a token with subject environment:demo, and exchange it against the Owner-capable deployer in three HTTP calls, going Reader to Owner. Nothing prevented this non-privileged execution context from invoking the privileged function. F7 is now CLOSED (Task 9): mls-verifier's federated credential is on a distinct environment:verify subject, and every verify job now declares environment: verify rather than environment: demo, so the OIDC token a verify job can mint no longer matches any credential federated to the deployer — the escalation primitive itself is removed, not merely made harder. verify-g0.ps1's Test-VerifierApp additionally asserts the verifier's subject is never shared with the deployer's, so a future misconfiguration reintroducing the collision fails G0 rather than passing silently. This control has no other open contributor (checked: no other finding cites 3.1.7).

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. (The verify/demo environment split and its Test-VerifierApp distinctness assertion, Task 9, are DONE.) Combined with F9's eventual diagnostic-logging fix, capturing OIDC token exchanges would make any future privileged-function execution auditable after the fact — a defense-in-depth addition, not a precondition for closing this control. A regression — environment: verify removed from a verify job, or the verifier re-federated to environment:demo — would reopen it.
